paragraphs.text: Some people argue that museums should charge for entry because visitors value what they pay for. I find this unconvincing. When a regional museum in my own city dropped its fee in 2015, visitor numbers doubled within a year, and the new visitors were not simply tourists: many were local families who had never been inside. Charging may raise money, but a museum that only the comfortable can afford has forgotten why it exists. That said, free entry is not free. Someone must pay for guards, heating and repairs, and I accept that governments will not always be willing to do so.
paragraphs.label: A
